Anti-Gravity Flight Control System: Measured Data Analysis of Five Technical Targets

01Data Sources and Verification Methodology

All data in this report comes from three independent sources, forming a triple cross-validation chain — every single number is traceable:

  • Formula-envelope reproduction — every metric is computed by open, reproducible pure-math formulas (strictly isomorphic to src/utils/flightPhysics.js and the back-end car_generator.flight_envelope); all chart curves in this report are pre-rendered as inline SVG from the same formulas, not hand-copied values;
  • Test-matrix lock — front-end vitest 285/285 (35 dedicated flight-physics cases) and back-end pytest 386 passed (14 flight-branch cases); formula regression, out-of-range clamping and the zero-geometry-change contract are all guarded by assertions;
  • Live verification on the public site — on 2026-10-16 a browser-automation agent completed full-flow interaction tests at https://evolution-ai.design/#/designer (see Chapter 09); real-time HUD readings matched offline formula results digit-for-digit.
Data Nature Boundary (Honest Disclosure)

This platform is a parametric design-simulation platform; the flight envelope is an engineering estimation model: curb mass is extrapolated from a 120 kg/m³ bounding-volume density, and the energy model is based on a disk-loading baseline with a sci-fi-bounded dark-energy/dark-matter analogy (η∈[0,0.3], field share ≤0.75). The data reflects the physical self-consistency of the design model and is not equivalent to real flight-test data; model honesty is guaranteed by the "honest degradation under extreme parameters" mechanism (end of Chapter 06).

02Theoretical Derivation of the Anti-Gravity Drive

The previous chapter established data credibility; this chapter answers the deeper question: where do these numbers come from. Every metric of the anti-gravity flight control — effective gravity, field-lift share, hover power, endurance multiple, peak factor, attitude envelope and latency — is analytically derived from three bounded assumptions (metric-shielding coefficient ηe, inertia-blending ratio ηcdm, disk-loading baseline) via classical mechanics, momentum theory and control theory, with no fitted black boxes. The six sections below follow the causal chain and provide the theoretical foundation for the five target measurements in Chapters 03–07.

2.1 Metric-shielding assumption and effective gravity (sci-fi bounded)

Dark energy exists as a negative-pressure state (equation of state w = −1); its engineering analogy is a local metric curvature established around the vehicle that shields the gravitational measure. The key trade-off is a "one-way" equivalence principle — the metric effect acts on gravitational measure only and leaves inertial mass unchanged: maneuvers and attitude responses still require real thrust, so all dynamic behavior remains physically self-consistent, with no runaway "vanishing inertia" scenario. The shielding coefficient is bounded to ηe∈[0, 0.3] (beyond which the shield boundary gradient destabilizes), and 0.35 is the coupling ceiling:

g_eff(η_e) = g·(1 − 0.35·η_e) (η_e∈[0,0.3] → g_eff ∈ [0.895g, g])
T/W = g / g_eff = 1/(1 − 0.35·η_e) ≥ 1 (necessary and sufficient hover condition; exactly 1.0 at η_e = 0)

2.2 Hover condition and the field–fan division of labor

Vertical force balance defines the system's first division of labor: the field carries the share, the fans retain the authority. Defining the field share s ≡ Lfield/Weff, its linear response s = 2.6·ηe + 1.8·ηcdm has ηe driving field-lift generation (first-order negative-pressure gradient response) and ηcdm contributing equivalent unloading under inertia shielding. The clamp s ≤ 0.75 is dictated by control theory, not energy: the field is the "slow channel" (metric establishment takes ~30 ms), so attitude bandwidth must come from the fast fan channel — retaining ≥25% of thrust for differential control is the very precondition of the ±2° attitude envelope.

2.3 The 1.5-power induced-power law and energy decomposition

The mathematical core of energy saving lies in momentum theory: hover induced power P ∝ T1.5/√(2ρA) (ideal actuator disk, blade quality factor folded into the baseline). When thrust drops to (1−s) of itself, power shrinks by (1−s)1.5 — this half-cubic law amplifies the benefit of "capping the field at 75%": at s = 0.75 the fan power retains only 0.251.5 = 12.5% of the baseline. Field maintenance is a different kind of term: sustaining the metric curvature pays for geometry, not external work, covering only coherence dissipation of 12 W/kg × s:

P_fan(s) = P_base·(1−s)^1.5 (momentum-theory half-cubic law, s=0.75 → ×0.125)
P_field = 12 W/kg · m · s (metric maintenance = coherence dissipation, not propulsive work)
P_base(m) = 55·(m/t)^1.2 kW (same-class lifting-fan disk-loading baseline; 1.2 = Reynolds/tip-loss empirical law)
P_hover = P_fan + P_field (sedan: 98.88×0.125 + 12×1630×0.75/1000 = 12.36 + 14.67 = 27.03 kW)

2.4 Closed-form endurance bound and the mass law

The equal-battery endurance multiple has a closed form E = Pbase/Phover. Substituting the decomposition reveals two structural conclusions. First, (1−s)1.5 = 0.125 (with s capped) gives a theoretical supremum of E → 1/0.125 = 8.0× at the zero-dissipation end; in practice the 12 W/kg dissipation dilutes it to 3.17–3.83. Second, Pbase ∝ m1.2 makes m/Pbase ∝ m−0.2 monotonically decreasing — the heavier the vehicle, the smaller the field-maintenance term relative to the baseline, and the higher E, which is the analytic origin of pickup (×3.83) exceeding sedan (×3.66) rather than a numerical coincidence:

E = P_base / P_hover = 1 / [ (1−s)^1.5 + 12·m·s / (1000·P_base) ]
P_base ∝ m^1.2 ⇒ m/P_base ∝ m^−0.2 (mass law: E rises monotonically with curb mass)
s = 0.688 (sport, uncapped) → E = 1/(0.1744 + 0.1410) = 3.17 (exactly the lowest of the six, see Chapter 06)

2.5 Analytic upper bound of the peak factor

"No significant energy peak" is not an empirical observation but a provable bound. At the takeoff instant only the fan thrust is multiplied by 1.2 (climb margin) while the field share is unchanged, so the peak always occurs at takeoff, never at hover. The peak factor is a weighted average of Pfan and Pfield: the pure-fan supremum is 1.21.5 = 1.3145, and the field-maintenance term (insensitive to fan thrust) dilutes it to 1.14–1.17 — the mathematical origin of the margin below the 1.25 limit. The turn differential adds only +5%, always below the takeoff increment:

P_takeoff = P_base·[1.2·(1−s)]^1.5 + P_field (fans ×1.2 only; field share unchanged)
Peak factor = P_takeoff / P_hover (supremum 1.2^1.5 = 1.3145 at P_field→0; diluted to 1.14–1.17 with field maintenance)

2.6 Over-damped loop, C² profiles and latency synthesis

The three attitude/kinematics criteria are equally provable. Over-damping: ζ = 1 + 0.6·ηcdm ≥ 1 renders the second-order attitude loop overshoot-free, with time constant τ = 1000/(ζ·2π·fn) = 63.7/ζ ms (fn = 2.5 Hz); recovery from an 8° gust back into the ±2° band is a monotonic exponential decay trec = τ·ln(8/2) = 88.3/ζ ms (78.8 ms at ζ = 1.12). C² profile: the quintic s(u) = 6u⁵ − 15u⁴ + 10u³ zeroes both endpoint velocity and acceleration — a cubic can only guarantee C¹, and an endpoint acceleration jump is felt as an impact; the peak slope 1.875 yields T = 1.875·|Δ|/45°/s. Latency synthesis: the larger of the command chain (perception + solving + field establishment, 30 + 6·nfans ms) and the recovery time:

ζ(η_cdm) = 1 + 0.6·η_cdm ≥ 1 (over-damped → zero overshoot → mathematical vertigo-free guarantee)
τ = 1000/(ζ·2π·2.5) = 63.7/ζ ms; t_rec = τ·ln(8/2) = 88.3/ζ ms (78.8 ms at ζ=1.12)
s(u) = 6u⁵ − 15u⁴ + 10u³, endpoint s′ = s″ = 0 (quintic C²; peak slope 1.875)
latency = max(30 + 6·n_fans, t_rec) ≤ 100 ms (verified across the full range: fans 2–8, η_cdm 0–0.3)

Chain closure: every criterion behind the five targets reduces to three bounded assumptions (ηe, ηcdm, disk-loading baseline) and four analytic formula groups (geff → s → Phover → quintic/ζ). Precisely because the metrics respond to parameters analytically, the self-consistency evidence in Chapter 06 ("sport uncapped → lowest endurance") and the honesty mechanism ("η zeroed → honest degradation") hold — they are not designed appearances but mathematical necessities of the model.

03Target 1: Hover Attitude Deviation ≤±2°

Hover attitude is guaranteed by an over-damped second-order loop: damping ratio ζ = 1 + 0.6·ηcdm ≥ 1 (dark-matter inertia blending), control bandwidth fn = 2.5 Hz, zero overshoot. Steady-state residual micro-sway uses a dual low-frequency sinusoid spectrum (0.07 / 0.11 Hz) with peak 0.85°/ζ — both frequencies far from the 0.5–1 Hz human motion-sickness band.

ζ = 1 + 0.6·η_cdm ≥ 1 (over-damped → zero overshoot)
θ(t) = (0.85/ζ)·[0.588·sin(2π·0.07t) + 0.412·sin(2π·0.11t + 1.3)] (deg)
gust recovery = τ·ln(8/2), τ = 1000/(ζ·2π·f_n) （ζ=1.12 → 78.8 ms）

Steady-state attitude peaks across the six types span 0.728°–0.767° (higher ηcdm → larger ζ → smaller sway), all within 36% of the ±2° envelope. In the 3D view the micro-sway is rendered with roll/pitch decoupling, its amplitude decaying with lift² progress and strictly zeroed on the ground.

04Target 2: Full-Freedom 360° Unlimited In-Place Turning

Yaw commands use a wrap-free accumulated angle design: consecutive commands accumulate across turns with no theoretical limit. The turn profile Δ·quintic(t/T) is a C²-continuous curve — endpoint angular velocity and acceleration are both zero, no jerking, no attitude destabilization; duration is computed from the 45°/s comfort-limited peak rate (T = 1.875·|Δ|/45), giving exactly 15.0 s for a full 360°.

T = 1.875·|Δ| / 45°/s (1.875 is the quintic mid-point peak slope; 2.5 s minimum transition)
ψ(t) = Δ·(6t⁵−15t⁴+10t³)/T⁵·… (quintic smoothstep, C² continuous)
peak turn rate = 1.875·Δ/T = 45°/s (within visual-rotation motion-sickness threshold)

In-place turning is achieved by fan differential torque — no centripetal acceleration, no roll coupling; roll and yaw are decoupled. Added power during turns is only +5% (differential increment), see the energy profile in Chapter 06. In the live test, after clicking the 360° button the vehicle rotated visibly and continuously within 5 s, smooth with no jumps.

05VTOL Profile: C² Smooth, Vertigo-Free

Lift altitude uses a quintic smoothstep h(t) = H·s(t/T) with strictly zero endpoint velocity and acceleration — no impact at takeoff or touchdown. Three vertigo-free guarantees accompany it: hover-bob amplitude <0.2% of vehicle length (≤9.2 mm), frequency <0.2 Hz, and zero camera roll throughout.

Preset hover altitudes span 1600–2000 mm and lift durations 2.8–3.8 s; the MPV takes the longest duration and highest altitude due to its greatest mass and size. Effective gravity geff = g·(1−0.35ηe) keeps the hover thrust-to-weight ratio at 1.052–1.083 — just above 1, matching the necessary-and-sufficient design where "the anti-gravity field carries the share while fans retain attitude-differential authority".

06Targets 3 + 4: Endurance ≥3× and No Energy Peaks in Any Regime

6.1 Energy Model

The core energy-saving logic of the anti-gravity route: the dark-energy negative-pressure field is a metric effect (geometric curvature), not propulsive work, with only ~12 W/kg of coherence dissipation; the conventional baseline uses a same-class high-efficiency lifting-fan disk-loading model Pbase = 55 kW/t1.2, with fan induced power shrinking by the 1.5th power of thrust.

field-lift share s = 2.6·η_e + 1.8·η_cdm ≤ 0.75 (fans retain ≥25% for attitude differential)
P_hover = P_base·(1−s)^1.5 + 12 W/kg·m·s (fans + field maintenance)
E = P_base / P_hover ≥ 3 (endurance multiple at equal battery; all six presets pass)

6.2 Endurance multiples across the six types

Multiples span 3.17×–3.83×. A notable self-consistency evidence: sport is the only type whose field share is not capped (0.688 < 0.75), and it also has the lowest endurance multiple — the model responds to parameters with physical consistency rather than a contrived "all green". At equal 100 kWh, sedan hover endurance extends from 1.01 h (conventional) to 3.70 h.

6.3 Energy peaks across all regimes

Honesty by Design: Honest Degradation at Extreme Parameters

When the user sets ηe and ηcdm to 0, the system honestly degrades to conventional-propulsion performance: field share goes to zero, endurance multiple falls back to ×1.0, peak factor rises to ×1.31 (exceeding the 1.25 limit), and the UI and back-end targets_met verdicts flip to false in sync — there is no "fudged pass" path; this behavior is locked by tests on both ends.

07Target 5: Flight Control Latency ≤100ms

Latency takes the larger of two chains: the command-chain latency (perception + solving + field establishment, 30 ms base + 6 ms per fan differential channel) and the large-disturbance recovery time (an 8° gust decaying back into the ±2° band, monotonic overshoot-free exponential decay τ·ln4 with ζ≥1).

Full-range verification: across 16 combinations of fans 2–8 and ηcdm 0–0.3, latency stays ≤100 ms (locked by vitest assertions). Mode transitions (takeoff ↔ hover ↔ turn ↔ landing) reuse the same C² profile mechanism — a transition command merely changes the profile target, no separate switching latency.

Cross-Validation Conclusion

The six real-time readings from the public HUD and metric cards are exactly identical to the offline formula envelope (27.03 kW / ×3.66 / ±0.76° / 79 ms / ×1.14 / 15.0 s) — proving front-end UI, formula layer and deployed artifact share one source, with no divergence between displayed and computed values.

10Conclusions, Boundaries and Next Steps

10.1 Conclusions

  • All five technical targets pass with design margin: attitude ±0.76° (2.6× margin), 360° turn 15.0 s (45°/s comfort limit), endurance ×3.17–3.83 (5.7% margin on the lowest), peak factor ×1.14–1.17 (limit 1.25), latency 76–80 ms (≥20 ms margin).
  • Path to the optimal balance: the anti-gravity sci-fi narrative is carried by the "capped field share + fan-differential floor" division of labor; lift/turn/landing motion profiles are unified by the C² quintic smoothstep; motion-sickness risk is locked down by over-damping ζ≥1 and low-frequency spectral constraints — algorithm (C² profiles), physics (metric-effect analogy), mathematics (bounded clamping), aerospace (thrust-to-weight sufficiency) and experience (triple vertigo-free guarantee) converge on one reproducible formula set.
  • Model honesty: the parameter→performance response is physically self-consistent (sport’s uncapped field share → lowest endurance; η zeroed → honest degradation to failing), and every verdict can be reproduced or overturned by the user in the UI in real time.

10.2 Boundaries

  • The data in this report is the output of an engineering estimation model of a design-simulation platform: the energy baseline (55 kW/t1.2), field-maintenance specific power (12 W/kg) and vehicle density (120 kg/m³) are model assumptions, not measurements from a real vehicle;
  • The dark-energy/dark-matter parameters are a "sci-fi bounded" analogy (η∈[0,0.3]), physically corresponding to an engineering abstraction of metric effects / inertia shielding;
  • "Measured" in this report means real-time computed readings of the deployed artifact verified in the public environment — not wind-tunnel or flight-test-grade measurement.

10.3 Next steps

  • Introduce gust-spectrum time-domain simulation (Dryden model) to replace the single 8° injection, refining the attitude-recovery time distribution;
  • Model battery C-rate constraints to output a true endurance–power envelope surface;
  • Field-interference analysis for multi-vehicle formation hovering and vertigo-free camera-following strategies.
